 Politics Taiwan Army drills response to acute combat stress
 564th Brigade rehearses helping a soldier regain composure after simulated shelling
   Oct. 26, 2026 17:09
 M1167 TOW missile Humvee during the Lusheng No. 2 exercise. (Military News agency photo)
 987 TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Taiwan’s Army practiced helping soldiers cope with acute battlefield stress during the Lusheng No. 2 exercise, which tested two brigades in prolonged simulated combat.
 In an ICOVER drill, a squad leader from the 564th Combined Arms Brigade followed prescribed steps to help a soldier regain composure and situational awareness, per  CNA . The soldier was portraying a combat exhaustion reaction following simulated artillery fire.
 Other casualty drills used electronic cards to record medical information for handovers. Troops evacuated simulated casualties to collection points for triage and emergency treatment.
 During day-and-night training, the 269th Combined Arms Brigade used successive defensive positions against the 564th’s northward advance. An ambush at the third defensive belt preceded a reversal of their offensive and defensive roles.
 Fuel trucks refueled the 269th’s M1A2T tanks at their positions before the vehicles continued on to the second defensive belt. Electronic warfare units rehearsed jamming and signal detection, while smoke screens covered troop movements.
 The military said its main training objectives had been achieved despite Typhoon Champi cutting short the Oct. 14–22 exercise, per  Liberty Times . Detailed combat losses were not disclosed, and no winner was announced.
